Different from commercial remote sensing processing software for satellite platforms, a serial of functions, including radiometric correction, geometric correction, image mosaic and fusion, are proposed referring to the feature of the aerial images. These functions can be freely composed to form a process pipeline with a friendly interactive user interface. Moreover, an automatic optimization method for processing pipeline is put forward based on the image quality evaluation. Besides, this system can yield valuable feedbacks to improve the imaging system. Its performance is verified by processing real aerial images. It is shown that the involved functional algorithms are robust against the instability of airborne platform, the variety of terrain, and other interfering factors resulting in imaging distortions.

articleTitle: A shadow removal method based on color model and undecimated wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: This paper proposed a shadow removal algorithm based on color model and undecimated wavelet transformation according to properties of the shadow and characters of each band. Firstly, the shadow area in original image was accurately extracted based on HSV color model. Secondly, Euclidean distance was used to determine the adjacent non-shadow area in order to compensate the shadow area. The statistics of shadow and non-shadow area was combined in undecimated wavelet transform to eliminate shadows. Finally, we compared our method with the algorithm based on HSI histogram equalization and RGB normalized. Experiment results showed that our method had better performance.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor image classification based on active learning
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: The insufficient number of training samples may often cause relatively low and unsteady accuracies in multi-sensor image classification. It is also difficult to properly deal with multi-source data simply by traditional classifiers. In this paper, we propose a novel active learning classification system to solve these problems. Firstly, the adaptive query by committee (AQBC) strategy could reduce the need of known labeled samples and meanwhile provide more accurate predictions of the actively selected unlabeled samples to further decrease misclassifying rates. In addition, the involved basic classifier based on the optimized Meta-Gaussian distribution could better fuse different types of feature sources. Finally, compared with other traditional methods, the experiment results show that the proposed classification system could improve classification accuracies effectively and make full use of the limited training samples in multi-source data sets.

articleTitle: Contour extraction improved by gradient saliency detection
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: The problem of accurately extraction of contour from cluttered natural scenes still remain to be solved. As traditional segmentation based on gradient map was facing a bottleneck in boundary detecting, according to the visual diversity of contour and texture in gradient map, we introduced visual attention and implemented saliency detection to enhance contour and inhibit texture. Experiment results showed that edge segmentation and detection based on gradient saliency map improved the performance of contour extraction, at the same time improved the robustness to parameter variation.

articleTitle: Pitch prediction in frequency domain for ITU-T G.719 audio codec
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: Pitch prediction in time domain is of great importance to improve the coding quality of speech. In this paper, we propose a method of frequency-domain pitch prediction for the full band ITU-T G.719 codec. The results of both the objective and the subjective evaluation show that the proposed method achieves higher reconstructed quality for the speech signal than the original method, especially for the lower coding rates.

articleTitle: Detection, extraction and quantitative measurement of atrophic regions on retinal surface in color fundus images
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: The problem of automatic detection and extraction of pathological images still remains an unsolved problem. The aim of this paper is to develop an automatic method for the detection, extraction and quantitative analysis of atrophic regions that occurred on retinal surface in retinal diseases. Its automatic quantification is important for determining disease progression and helpful for clinical diagnosis of disease. The paper utilized an adaptive threshold for various regions of color fundus image which determined simply by different blocking models. The algorithm is computationally efficient and fast. Quantitative evaluation experiments on 300 color fundus images show a mean sensitivity/specificity of 98.7/96.6 % for our approach.

articleTitle: An extensible FPGA-based postprocessor architecture of timing skew correction for time-interleaved ADCs
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: An extensible postprocessor architecture of a new algorithm is presented in this paper to correct the timing skew in 7-channel time-interleaved ADCs. The Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithm is utilized to identify the timing skew, which is used to compensate digital output according to its high order Taylor expansion. FPGA synthesis results show that, with±0.02Ts timing skew, and normalized input frequency fin/fs=0.47, signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio and spurious-free dynamic range of the TIADC after calibration reach 85.7dB and 96.8dB, improved by 50dB and 54dB respectively, compared to the uncalibrated digital outputs. The circuit based on the proposed architecture is simple and easily extensive to TIADC with different number of split-ADCs.

articleTitle: Motion capture and reconstruction based on depth information using Kinect
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: In this paper, a novel technique which provides visual feedback to the trainee in a 3D virtual environment is proposed. This method contains two steps. Firstly, the real-time depth data for the 3D human motions are captured using Kinect (a latest depth sensor launched by Microsoft) and then those depth dada are converted into key-node data of human skeletons. Next, 3D human body movements are reconstructed by combining these key-node data and personalized virtual models of human body created by the open source software of “MakeHuman”. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can obtain a fairly accurate estimation of the real-time 3D human body movements.

articleTitle: An image reconstruction approach in discrete cosine transform domain
publicationTitle: 2012 5th International Congress on Image and Signal Processing
abstract: Image super-resolution in compressed domain is a topic of interest for many applications. In this paper, the relationships of DCT(discrete cosine transform) coefficients between high-resolution images and its low resolution counterparts are explored, a simple reconstruction approach is proposed based on these analysis. Simulation results showed that the derivation is correct and proposed approach can achieve image reconstruction in DCT-domain directly with lower time consuming than traditional treatment. The result in this paper has somewhat significance in compressed-domain image superresolution and other applications.
